headline: A Boston Globe opinion essay argues that college applications sound like AI because students have been taught the same essay formulas for years.
score_reason: Matches pool score; opinion piece, kept at 5 for its relevance to admissions season.
importance_line: It matters to applicants and parents facing AI-detector flags, but this is one tutor's argument, not research.
summary: In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, Ben Urwand, who runs the college-essay tutoring service Real College Essays, argues that applicant essays have become alike over about 20 years of online advice, so AI imitates them and detectors flag human writing. He says the fix is for colleges to reward essays that show a student's own thinking, not a tidy lesson.
notes: Opinion; author's business interest disclosed in summary.
